house.description: Requirement for counties to fund ARMER network expansion eliminated, state funding for public safety radio communications infrastructure established, framework for collaboration and interoperability across law enforcement jurisdictions established, and money appropriated.

House.text: Introduction and first reading, referred to Public Safety Finance and Policy

bill_text.text_with_changes:
A bill for an act relating to public safety; eliminating requirement for counties to fund ARMER network expansion; establishing state funding for public safety radio communications infrastructure; establishing framework for collaboration and interoperability across law enforcement jurisdictions; requiring reports; authorizing rulemaking; appropriating money; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 403.21, by adding subdivisions; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 403.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1. [+SHORT TITLE. +]

[+This act may be cited as the "Minnesota Public Safety Radio Communications Funding and Interoperability Act." +]

Sec. 2.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 403.21, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

[+Subd. 1b.+]

[+Cost-share arrangement.+]

[+"Cost-share arrangement" means a funding mechanism whereby the state and participating local jurisdictions share the costs of public safety communications infrastructure according to a predetermined formula. +]

Sec. 3.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 403.21, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

[+Subd. 3a.+]

[+Interoperability.+]

[+"Interoperability" means the ability of public safety agencies to communicate with each other in real time using voice and data systems and exchange and use information on demand. +]

Sec. 4.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 403.21, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

[+Subd. 5a.+]

[+Network expansion.+]

[+"Network expansion" means the acquisition, construction, installation, upgrading, or enhancement of communications towers, equipment, infrastructure, or technology related to the ARMER network or other public safety radio communications systems. +]

Sec. 5.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 403.21, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

[+Subd. 7b.+]

[+Public safety agency.+]

[+"Public safety agency" means any federal, state, local, or Tribal agency providing law enforcement, fire, emergency medical, emergency management, or public works services. +]

Sec. 6.

[+[403.265] STATE FUNDING FOR ARMER NETWORK. +]

[+Subdivision 1.+]

[+Elimination of county funding requirement.+]

[+(a) Notwithstanding any other law to the contrary, no county is required to fund, through property taxes or other local revenue sources, the expansion, enhancement, or maintenance of the ARMER network. +]

[+(b) This subdivision does not prohibit voluntary participation by counties in cost-share arrangements as provided in subdivision 3. +]

[+Subd. 2.+]

[+Public safety radio communications infrastructure account.+]

[+(a) The public safety radio communications infrastructure account is created in the special revenue fund to support the ARMER network and related interoperable communications systems. The commissioners of public safety and transportation must administer the account in collaboration with the Statewide Emergency Communications Board. +]

[+(b) Money in the account consists of money as provided by law, dedicated revenue sources, and any other money donated, allotted, transferred, or otherwise provided to the account. +]

[+(c) Money in the account must only be used for: +]

[+(1) capital costs associated with ARMER network expansion and enhancement; +]

[+(2) maintenance and operational costs of the ARMER network; +]

[+(3) technology upgrades to ensure system reliability and interoperability; +]

[+(4) training and technical assistance related to public safety communications; and +]

[+(5) the Statewide Emergency Communications Board committees. +]

[+(d) Annually by ......, the commissioner of public safety must provide a report to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with jurisdiction over public safety detailing account revenues and expenditures and the status of ARMER network deployment and enhancement. +]

[+Subd. 3.+]

[+Optional cost-share program.+]

[+(a) The commissioners of public safety and transportation, in consultation with the Statewide Emergency Communications Board, may establish cost-share arrangements with local governments or Tribal governments for specific network expansion projects. +]

[+(b) Cost-share arrangements must: +]

[+(1) be voluntary and based on mutual agreement; +]

[+(2) provide clear financial benefits to participating local jurisdictions; +]

[+(3) not require local jurisdictions to contribute more than 25 percent of total project costs; and +]

[+(4) include provisions ensuring the state covers ongoing maintenance costs. +]

[+(c) The Statewide Emergency Communications Board must develop guidelines for cost-share arrangements, including application procedures, eligible projects, and cost-allocation formulas. +]

[+(d) Priority consideration in cost-share arrangements must be given to: +]

[+(1) projects enhancing interoperability across multiple jurisdictions; +]

[+(2) underserved areas lacking adequate public safety communications coverage; +]

[+(3) projects demonstrating regional collaboration; and +]

[+(4) jurisdictions with demonstrated financial hardship. +]

[+EFFECTIVE DATE.+]

[+Subdivision 1 is effective the day following final enactment. Subdivisions 2 and 3 are effective July 1, 2026. +]

Sec. 7. [+STATE FUNDING FOR ARMER NETWORK; IMPLEMENTATION. +]

[+Subdivision 1.+]

[+Transition provisions.+]

[+(a) Within 270 days of the effective date of this section, the commissioner of public safety must: +]

[+(1) develop a transition plan for assuming financial responsibility for ongoing and planned projects; +]

[+(2) review all existing agreements requiring counties to fund ARMER network expansion; +]

[+(3) negotiate amendments or replacements to such agreements to conform with this section; and +]

[+(4) identify any statutory or regulatory changes needed to implement this section. +]

[+(b) Counties are not required to make any additional capital contributions for ARMER network expansion after the effective date of this section, provided that counties are responsible for payments due under existing bonded indebtedness until such obligations are satisfied or refinanced by the state. +]

[+(c) The commissioner may negotiate with counties to assume outstanding debt obligations related to ARMER network expansion, subject to available appropriations. +]

[+Subd. 2.+]

[+Rulemaking authority.+]

[+(a) The commissioner of public safety may adopt rules to implement state funding for the ARMER network under Minnesota Statutes, section 403.265, including rules governing: +]

[+(1) administration of the public safety radio communications infrastructure account; +]

[+(2) cost-share arrangement procedures and formulas; +]

[+(3) grant application and award processes; +]

[+(4) reporting requirements for grant recipients; and +]

[+(5) other matters necessary to carry out the purposes of this act. +]

[+(b) Rules adopted under this subdivision are subject to Minnesota Statutes, chapter 14. +]

[+Subd. 3.+]

[+Technical assistance.+]

[+The commissioner of public safety must provide technical assistance to local jurisdictions on: +]

[+(1) transitioning to state-funded ARMER network infrastructure; +]

[+(2) achieving interoperability standards; +]

[+(3) accessing grant money and cost-share programs; +]

[+(4) implementing collaborative response protocols; and +]

[+(5) training personnel on interoperable communications systems. +]

[+Subd. 4.+]

[+Coordination with federal agencies.+]

[+The commissioner of public safety must coordinate with federal agencies to: +]

[+(1) maximize federal funding opportunities for public safety communications; +]

[+(2) ensure state systems comply with federal interoperability standards; +]

[+(3) participate in national public safety communications initiatives; and +]

[+(4) share best practices with other states and jurisdictions. +]

[+EFFECTIVE DATE.+]

[+This section is effective the day following final enactment. +]

Sec. 8. [+PUBLIC SAFETY RADIO COMMUNICATIONS DEDICATED REVENUE SOURCES; TAX RELIEF; REPORT. +]

[+Subdivision 1.+]

[+Dedicated revenue sources; report.+]

[+(a) The legislature must consider establishing dedicated revenue sources for the public safety radio communications infrastructure account established in Minnesota Statutes, section 403.265, which may include the following: +]

[+(1) surcharges on telecommunications services; +]

[+(2) fees; +]

[+(3) federal grants and matching money; +]

[+(4) revenue from state asset forfeitures designated for public safety purposes; or +]

[+(5) other revenue sources deemed appropriate. +]

[+(b) The commissioner of public safety must study potential dedicated revenue sources for the public safety radio communications infrastructure account established in Minnesota Statutes, section 403.265, including but not limited to the potential dedicated revenue sources in paragraph (a), and submit a report of recommendations to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with jurisdiction over public safety by December 31, 2026. +]

[+Subd. 2.+]

[+County tax relief.+]

[+The legislature recognizes that counties will realize significant property tax relief as a result of eliminating the requirement to fund ARMER network expansion under Minnesota Statutes, section 403.265, subdivision 1. Therefore, counties are encouraged to reinvest cost savings into local public safety priorities, including but not limited to: +]

[+(1) law enforcement personnel and equipment; +]

[+(2) crime prevention and community policing programs; +]

[+(3) mental health crisis response services; +]

[+(4) emergency management capabilities; or +]

[+(5) other public safety needs identified by the county. +]

[+EFFECTIVE DATE.+]

[+This section is effective the day following final enactment. +]

Sec. 9. [+PUBLIC SAFETY RADIO COMMUNICATIONS INFRASTRUCTURE ACCOUNT; APPROPRIATION. +]

[+$....... in fiscal year 2026 and $....... in fiscal year 2027 are appropriated from the general fund to the commissioner of public safety for deposit in the public safety radio communications infrastructure account established in Minnesota Statutes, section 403.265. +]

[+EFFECTIVE DATE.+]

[+This section is effective the day following final enactment. +]

Sec. 10. [+REVISOR INSTRUCTION. +]

[+The revisor of statutes must renumber the subdivisions in Minnesota Statutes, section 403.21, so that the terms appear in alphabetical order and make necessary cross-reference changes consistent with the renumbering. +]
bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to public safety; eliminating requirement for counties to fund ARMER network expansion; establishing state funding for public safety radio communications infrastructure; establishing framework for collaboration and interoperability across law enforcement jurisdictions; requiring reports; authorizing rulemaking; appropriating money; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 403.21, by adding subdivisions; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 403.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1. SHORT TITLE.

This act may be cited as the "Minnesota Public Safety Radio Communications Funding and Interoperability Act."

Sec. 2.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 403.21, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

Subd. 1b.

Cost-share arrangement.

"Cost-share arrangement" means a funding mechanism whereby the state and participating local jurisdictions share the costs of public safety communications infrastructure according to a predetermined formula.

Sec. 3.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 403.21, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

Subd. 3a.

Interoperability.

"Interoperability" means the ability of public safety agencies to communicate with each other in real time using voice and data systems and exchange and use information on demand.

Sec. 4.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 403.21, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

Subd. 5a.

Network expansion.

"Network expansion" means the acquisition, construction, installation, upgrading, or enhancement of communications towers, equipment, infrastructure, or technology related to the ARMER network or other public safety radio communications systems.

Sec. 5.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 403.21, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

Subd. 7b.

Public safety agency.

"Public safety agency" means any federal, state, local, or Tribal agency providing law enforcement, fire, emergency medical, emergency management, or public works services.

Sec. 6.

[403.265] STATE FUNDING FOR ARMER NETWORK.

Subdivision 1.

Elimination of county funding requirement.

(a) Notwithstanding any other law to the contrary, no county is required to fund, through property taxes or other local revenue sources, the expansion, enhancement, or maintenance of the ARMER network.

(b) This subdivision does not prohibit voluntary participation by counties in cost-share arrangements as provided in subdivision 3.

Subd. 2.

Public safety radio communications infrastructure account.

(a) The public safety radio communications infrastructure account is created in the special revenue fund to support the ARMER network and related interoperable communications systems. The commissioners of public safety and transportation must administer the account in collaboration with the Statewide Emergency Communications Board.

(b) Money in the account consists of money as provided by law, dedicated revenue sources, and any other money donated, allotted, transferred, or otherwise provided to the account.

(c) Money in the account must only be used for:

(1) capital costs associated with ARMER network expansion and enhancement;

(2) maintenance and operational costs of the ARMER network;

(3) technology upgrades to ensure system reliability and interoperability;

(4) training and technical assistance related to public safety communications; and

(5) the Statewide Emergency Communications Board committees.

(d) Annually by ......, the commissioner of public safety must provide a report to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with jurisdiction over public safety detailing account revenues and expenditures and the status of ARMER network deployment and enhancement.

Subd. 3.

Optional cost-share program.

(a) The commissioners of public safety and transportation, in consultation with the Statewide Emergency Communications Board, may establish cost-share arrangements with local governments or Tribal governments for specific network expansion projects.

(b) Cost-share arrangements must:

(1) be voluntary and based on mutual agreement;

(2) provide clear financial benefits to participating local jurisdictions;

(3) not require local jurisdictions to contribute more than 25 percent of total project costs; and

(4) include provisions ensuring the state covers ongoing maintenance costs.

(c) The Statewide Emergency Communications Board must develop guidelines for cost-share arrangements, including application procedures, eligible projects, and cost-allocation formulas.

(d) Priority consideration in cost-share arrangements must be given to:

(1) projects enhancing interoperability across multiple jurisdictions;

(2) underserved areas lacking adequate public safety communications coverage;

(3) projects demonstrating regional collaboration; and

(4) jurisdictions with demonstrated financial hardship.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

Subdivision 1 is effective the day following final enactment. Subdivisions 2 and 3 are effective July 1, 2026.

Sec. 7. STATE FUNDING FOR ARMER NETWORK; IMPLEMENTATION.

Subdivision 1.

Transition provisions.

(a) Within 270 days of the effective date of this section, the commissioner of public safety must:

(1) develop a transition plan for assuming financial responsibility for ongoing and planned projects;

(2) review all existing agreements requiring counties to fund ARMER network expansion;

(3) negotiate amendments or replacements to such agreements to conform with this section; and

(4) identify any statutory or regulatory changes needed to implement this section.

(b) Counties are not required to make any additional capital contributions for ARMER network expansion after the effective date of this section, provided that counties are responsible for payments due under existing bonded indebtedness until such obligations are satisfied or refinanced by the state.

(c) The commissioner may negotiate with counties to assume outstanding debt obligations related to ARMER network expansion, subject to available appropriations.

Subd. 2.

Rulemaking authority.

(a) The commissioner of public safety may adopt rules to implement state funding for the ARMER network under Minnesota Statutes, section 403.265, including rules governing:

(1) administration of the public safety radio communications infrastructure account;

(2) cost-share arrangement procedures and formulas;

(3) grant application and award processes;

(4) reporting requirements for grant recipients; and

(5) other matters necessary to carry out the purposes of this act.

(b) Rules adopted under this subdivision are subject to Minnesota Statutes, chapter 14.

Subd. 3.

Technical assistance.

The commissioner of public safety must provide technical assistance to local jurisdictions on:

(1) transitioning to state-funded ARMER network infrastructure;

(2) achieving interoperability standards;

(3) accessing grant money and cost-share programs;

(4) implementing collaborative response protocols; and

(5) training personnel on interoperable communications systems.

Subd. 4.

Coordination with federal agencies.

The commissioner of public safety must coordinate with federal agencies to:

(1) maximize federal funding opportunities for public safety communications;

(2) ensure state systems comply with federal interoperability standards;

(3) participate in national public safety communications initiatives; and

(4) share best practices with other states and jurisdictions.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective the day following final enactment.

Sec. 8. PUBLIC SAFETY RADIO COMMUNICATIONS DEDICATED REVENUE SOURCES; TAX RELIEF; REPORT.

Subdivision 1.

Dedicated revenue sources; report.

(a) The legislature must consider establishing dedicated revenue sources for the public safety radio communications infrastructure account established in Minnesota Statutes, section 403.265, which may include the following:

(1) surcharges on telecommunications services;

(2) fees;

(3) federal grants and matching money;

(4) revenue from state asset forfeitures designated for public safety purposes; or

(5) other revenue sources deemed appropriate.

(b) The commissioner of public safety must study potential dedicated revenue sources for the public safety radio communications infrastructure account established in Minnesota Statutes, section 403.265, including but not limited to the potential dedicated revenue sources in paragraph (a), and submit a report of recommendations to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with jurisdiction over public safety by December 31, 2026.

Subd. 2.

County tax relief.

The legislature recognizes that counties will realize significant property tax relief as a result of eliminating the requirement to fund ARMER network expansion under Minnesota Statutes, section 403.265, subdivision 1. Therefore, counties are encouraged to reinvest cost savings into local public safety priorities, including but not limited to:

(1) law enforcement personnel and equipment;

(2) crime prevention and community policing programs;

(3) mental health crisis response services;

(4) emergency management capabilities; or

(5) other public safety needs identified by the county.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective the day following final enactment.

Sec. 9. PUBLIC SAFETY RADIO COMMUNICATIONS INFRASTRUCTURE ACCOUNT; APPROPRIATION.

$....... in fiscal year 2026 and $....... in fiscal year 2027 are appropriated from the general fund to the commissioner of public safety for deposit in the public safety radio communications infrastructure account established in Minnesota Statutes, section 403.265.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective the day following final enactment.

Sec. 10. REVISOR INSTRUCTION.

The revisor of statutes must renumber the subdivisions in Minnesota Statutes, section 403.21, so that the terms appear in alphabetical order and make necessary cross-reference changes consistent with the renumbering.

bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to public safety; eliminating requirement for counties to fund ARMER network expansion; establishing state funding for public safety radio communications infrastructure; establishing framework for collaboration and interoperability across law enforcement jurisdictions; requiring reports; authorizing rulemaking; appropriating money; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 403.21, by adding subdivisions; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 403.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1. SHORT TITLE.

This act may be cited as the "Minnesota Public Safety Radio Communications Funding and Interoperability Act."

Sec. 2.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 403.21, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

Subd. 1b.

Cost-share arrangement.

"Cost-share arrangement" means a funding mechanism whereby the state and participating local jurisdictions share the costs of public safety communications infrastructure according to a predetermined formula.

Sec. 3.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 403.21, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

Subd. 3a.

Interoperability.

"Interoperability" means the ability of public safety agencies to communicate with each other in real time using voice and data systems and exchange and use information on demand.

Sec. 4.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 403.21, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

Subd. 5a.

Network expansion.

"Network expansion" means the acquisition, construction, installation, upgrading, or enhancement of communications towers, equipment, infrastructure, or technology related to the ARMER network or other public safety radio communications systems.

Sec. 5.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 403.21, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

Subd. 7b.

Public safety agency.

"Public safety agency" means any federal, state, local, or Tribal agency providing law enforcement, fire, emergency medical, emergency management, or public works services.

Sec. 6.

[403.265] STATE FUNDING FOR ARMER NETWORK.

Subdivision 1.

Elimination of county funding requirement.

(a) Notwithstanding any other law to the contrary, no county is required to fund, through property taxes or other local revenue sources, the expansion, enhancement, or maintenance of the ARMER network.

(b) This subdivision does not prohibit voluntary participation by counties in cost-share arrangements as provided in subdivision 3.

Subd. 2.

Public safety radio communications infrastructure account.

(a) The public safety radio communications infrastructure account is created in the special revenue fund to support the ARMER network and related interoperable communications systems. The commissioners of public safety and transportation must administer the account in collaboration with the Statewide Emergency Communications Board.

(b) Money in the account consists of money as provided by law, dedicated revenue sources, and any other money donated, allotted, transferred, or otherwise provided to the account.

(c) Money in the account must only be used for:

(1) capital costs associated with ARMER network expansion and enhancement;

(2) maintenance and operational costs of the ARMER network;

(3) technology upgrades to ensure system reliability and interoperability;

(4) training and technical assistance related to public safety communications; and

(5) the Statewide Emergency Communications Board committees.

(d) Annually by ......, the commissioner of public safety must provide a report to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with jurisdiction over public safety detailing account revenues and expenditures and the status of ARMER network deployment and enhancement.

Subd. 3.

Optional cost-share program.

(a) The commissioners of public safety and transportation, in consultation with the Statewide Emergency Communications Board, may establish cost-share arrangements with local governments or Tribal governments for specific network expansion projects.

(b) Cost-share arrangements must:

(1) be voluntary and based on mutual agreement;

(2) provide clear financial benefits to participating local jurisdictions;

(3) not require local jurisdictions to contribute more than 25 percent of total project costs; and

(4) include provisions ensuring the state covers ongoing maintenance costs.

(c) The Statewide Emergency Communications Board must develop guidelines for cost-share arrangements, including application procedures, eligible projects, and cost-allocation formulas.

(d) Priority consideration in cost-share arrangements must be given to:

(1) projects enhancing interoperability across multiple jurisdictions;

(2) underserved areas lacking adequate public safety communications coverage;

(3) projects demonstrating regional collaboration; and

(4) jurisdictions with demonstrated financial hardship.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

Subdivision 1 is effective the day following final enactment. Subdivisions 2 and 3 are effective July 1, 2026.

Sec. 7. STATE FUNDING FOR ARMER NETWORK; IMPLEMENTATION.

Subdivision 1.

Transition provisions.

(a) Within 270 days of the effective date of this section, the commissioner of public safety must:

(1) develop a transition plan for assuming financial responsibility for ongoing and planned projects;

(2) review all existing agreements requiring counties to fund ARMER network expansion;

(3) negotiate amendments or replacements to such agreements to conform with this section; and

(4) identify any statutory or regulatory changes needed to implement this section.

(b) Counties are not required to make any additional capital contributions for ARMER network expansion after the effective date of this section, provided that counties are responsible for payments due under existing bonded indebtedness until such obligations are satisfied or refinanced by the state.

(c) The commissioner may negotiate with counties to assume outstanding debt obligations related to ARMER network expansion, subject to available appropriations.

Subd. 2.

Rulemaking authority.

(a) The commissioner of public safety may adopt rules to implement state funding for the ARMER network under Minnesota Statutes, section 403.265, including rules governing:

(1) administration of the public safety radio communications infrastructure account;

(2) cost-share arrangement procedures and formulas;

(3) grant application and award processes;

(4) reporting requirements for grant recipients; and

(5) other matters necessary to carry out the purposes of this act.

(b) Rules adopted under this subdivision are subject to Minnesota Statutes, chapter 14.

Subd. 3.

Technical assistance.

The commissioner of public safety must provide technical assistance to local jurisdictions on:

(1) transitioning to state-funded ARMER network infrastructure;

(2) achieving interoperability standards;

(3) accessing grant money and cost-share programs;

(4) implementing collaborative response protocols; and

(5) training personnel on interoperable communications systems.

Subd. 4.

Coordination with federal agencies.

The commissioner of public safety must coordinate with federal agencies to:

(1) maximize federal funding opportunities for public safety communications;

(2) ensure state systems comply with federal interoperability standards;

(3) participate in national public safety communications initiatives; and

(4) share best practices with other states and jurisdictions.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective the day following final enactment.

Sec. 8. PUBLIC SAFETY RADIO COMMUNICATIONS DEDICATED REVENUE SOURCES; TAX RELIEF; REPORT.

Subdivision 1.

Dedicated revenue sources; report.

(a) The legislature must consider establishing dedicated revenue sources for the public safety radio communications infrastructure account established in Minnesota Statutes, section 403.265, which may include the following:

(1) surcharges on telecommunications services;

(2) fees;

(3) federal grants and matching money;

(4) revenue from state asset forfeitures designated for public safety purposes; or

(5) other revenue sources deemed appropriate.

(b) The commissioner of public safety must study potential dedicated revenue sources for the public safety radio communications infrastructure account established in Minnesota Statutes, section 403.265, including but not limited to the potential dedicated revenue sources in paragraph (a), and submit a report of recommendations to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with jurisdiction over public safety by December 31, 2026.

Subd. 2.

County tax relief.

The legislature recognizes that counties will realize significant property tax relief as a result of eliminating the requirement to fund ARMER network expansion under Minnesota Statutes, section 403.265, subdivision 1. Therefore, counties are encouraged to reinvest cost savings into local public safety priorities, including but not limited to:

(1) law enforcement personnel and equipment;

(2) crime prevention and community policing programs;

(3) mental health crisis response services;

(4) emergency management capabilities; or

(5) other public safety needs identified by the county.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective the day following final enactment.

Sec. 9. PUBLIC SAFETY RADIO COMMUNICATIONS INFRASTRUCTURE ACCOUNT; APPROPRIATION.

$....... in fiscal year 2026 and $....... in fiscal year 2027 are appropriated from the general fund to the commissioner of public safety for deposit in the public safety radio communications infrastructure account established in Minnesota Statutes, section 403.265.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective the day following final enactment.

Sec. 10. REVISOR INSTRUCTION.

The revisor of statutes must renumber the subdivisions in Minnesota Statutes, section 403.21, so that the terms appear in alphabetical order and make necessary cross-reference changes consistent with the renumbering.
